item.title: Follow an editor’s distinction between silence and refusal
item.summary: Two editors discuss how to report an unanswered invitation without ascribing intent.
item.transcript_text:
Editor: You write that the former director declined to comment. Our log shows two messages to the public office and an unverified phone number.
Reporter: Nobody got back to me, and they had a full week.
Editor: A week tells us the time allowed. It doesn't tell us who saw the request or whether they deliberately withheld an answer. Say we hadn't received a reply by publication. Put the offer of a follow-up beside that line.
Reporter: Won't it weaken the account of the original decision?
Editor: The signed minutes establish the decision. The gap is the director's account of why it happened. If the minutes are inconsistent, that's a separate finding.
Reporter: Then I'll put the unanswered question beside what the minutes can establish.

options: It rules out a later reply
It implies a deliberate decision that has not been established
It reveals a private number
It contradicts an explicit refusal in the log
questions.explanation: An unanswered request does not establish that the recipient chose not to answer.

questions.prompt: What does the full week establish?
options: The amount of time allowed
Confirmed receipt on the first day
Enough time regardless of the circumstances
That a follow-up would be pointless
questions.explanation: The wait is documented, while receipt and intent are unresolved.

questions.prompt: What remains well supported if the line changes?
options: Why the director personally favoured the decision
That no one in the office received the request
That the minutes contain contradictions
That the recorded decision was taken
questions.explanation: Signed minutes support occurrence, independent of personal explanation.

questions.prompt: Why include the offer of follow-up?
options: To promise the story will be removed later
To replace the original contact effort
To show the account can still be supplemented
To discredit the signed minutes
questions.explanation: The editor wants to avoid implying the question is closed.

questions.prompt: How will the reporter revise the structure?
options: Move the uncertainty away from the decision
Put the open question next to the documentary finding it qualifies
Replace the minutes with a description of the contact log
Make silence the lead finding
questions.explanation: The last line places the unanswered question beside the evidence’s scope.

children.segment_text: a week tells us the time allowed
